subject: Archaeology
title: Schliemann Finds Troy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Schliemann Finds Troy usable.

hook.text: Everyone said Troy was a myth. Heinrich Schliemann bet his fortune it was real — and started digging.

buildup.text: Using Homer's Iliad as a guide, Schliemann identified a hill in Turkey called Hisarlik in 1868.

discovery.text: He found not one city but nine, layered on top of each other across thousands of years.

twist.text: Schliemann blasted through layers with dynamite, destroying priceless evidence in his rush for gold.

climax.text: He claimed to find Priam's treasure, but it came from a city 1,000 years older than Homer's Troy.

punchline.text: He found Troy but destroyed much of it in the process.

quiz.question: What major mistake did Schliemann make while excavating Troy?
options: He dug at the wrong site entirely
He destroyed layers with dynamite, losing priceless evidence
He refused to share his findings with other scholars

details.summary: Heinrich Schliemann, a self-taught businessman turned archaeologist, excavated Hisarlik in Turkey in the 1870s and claimed to have found Homer's Troy. Though his methods were destructive and his identifications often wrong, he proved that Troy was a real place, not just a myth.
details.whyItMatters: Schliemann demonstrated that literary texts could guide archaeological discovery. Despite his many errors — including destroying the actual Homeric layer — he established that myth and archaeology could intersect productively.
takeaways: Schliemann excavated Hisarlik, Turkey, identifying it as ancient Troy
His destructive methods damaged the very layers he sought
He proved Troy was real, transforming how myth and archaeology relate

faq.question: Did Schliemann actually find Homer's Troy?
faq.answer: He found the site of Troy but misidentified the layer. The gold treasure he called Priam's Treasure came from a city 1,000 years too early. Later excavators identified Troy VIIa as the likely candidate for the Homeric city, dating to around 1200 BCE.

faq.question: Why are Schliemann's methods criticized?
faq.answer: He dug trenches straight through occupation layers, destroying archaeological context. He removed artifacts without proper recording and secretly exported the gold treasure to Germany. Modern archaeologists view him as a pioneering but deeply flawed figure.
